fable.w: This section only makes technical amendments that shift administrative authority from the President to the Secretary of Agriculture and set funding levels from the Commodity Credit Corporation. The tempting reading is that references to a "Federal agency assisting" imply coordination, but that is purely intra-governmental. No outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue or object.
fable.s: by striking “President” each place it appears and inserting “Secretary”

opus.w: This section only moves program authority from the President to the Secretary and updates funding amounts and fiscal years. Every actor it mentions (the President, the Secretary, the Department of Agriculture, other federal agencies, the Commodity Credit Corporation) is inside the federal government. The underlying program may involve outside organizations, but this text creates no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue for anyone outside the government.
opus.s: by striking “The President shall designate 1 or more Federal agencies” and inserting “The Secretary shall”
opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through.** The tempting reading is that the underlying McGovern-Dole Food for Education program (7 U.S.C. 1736o–1) works with outside groups such as private voluntary organizations, so changing who runs it might look like participation. That fails because this section only makes technical changes: it moves authority from the President to the Secretary, and it changes funding amounts and fiscal years. Nothing in the text brings anyone outside the federal government into a federal decision. The only actors named are the President, the Secretary, the Department of Agriculture, other federal agencies and the Commodity Credit Corporation, all of which are inside the federal government.

2. **Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section merely amends statutory text to change which federal official or agency is responsible for certain actions (shifting authority from the President to the Secretary of Agriculture). It does not create any process for consulting with or coordinating with non-federal entities. It looks like participation because it involves the Secretary of Agriculture making decisions and using funds.
qwen_chat.s: Section 3107 of the Farm Security and Rural Investment Act of 2002 (7 U.S.C. 1736o–1) is amended— (1) in subsections (b), (c)(2)(B), (f)(1), (h), (i), and (l)(1), by striking “President” each place it appears and inserting “Secretary”; (2) in subsection (d), by striking “The President shall designate 1 or more Federal agencies” and inserting “The Secretary shall”; (3) in paragraph (f)(2), by striking “implementing agency” and inserting “Secretary”; and (4) in subsection (l)— (A) by striking paragraph (1) and inserting the following:“(1) Use of commodity credit corporation funds.—Of the funds of the Commodity Credit Corporation, the Secretary shall use to carry out this section $84,000,000 for fiscal year 2009, to remain available until expended.”; (B) in paragraph (2), by striking “2004 through 2007” and inserting “2008 through 2012”; and (C) in paragraph (3), by striking “any Federal agency implementing or assisting” and inserting “the Department of Agriculture or any other Federal agency assisting”.
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it involves the Secretary of Agriculture making decisions and using funds.
Resolution: This section merely amends statutory text to change which federal official or agency is responsible for certain actions (shifting authority from the President to the Secretary of Agriculture). It does not create any process for consulting with or coordinating with non-federal entities.
